title: BENKEI
subtitle: the monk who wouldn't fall
source: Gikeiki (Benkei and Ushiwakamaru; Sojobo of Kurama); Noh 'Ataka' / kabuki 'Kanjincho'; Battle of Koromogawa 1189, Benkei no tachi-ojo; idiom 'Benkei no nakidokoro' (the shin); Meiji-era Yoshitsune = Genghis Khan theory (Suematsu Kencho 1879)

lines.say: [nervous] Kon... why won't that whole army cross the bridge?
cap: Kon... why won't that whole army

lines.say: [quiet] Because of him.
[incredulous] He's ONE guy!
[low, grave] He's been dead... for an hour.
[shocked] WHAT?!
[storytelling] That's Benkei. To understand him, we go back to another bridge. In Kyoto.
cap: we go back to another bridge.

lines.say: A giant warrior monk. Seven weapons on his back.
He vowed to beat a thousand samurai on that bridge... and take every one of their swords.
cap: and take every one of their {o:swords}.

lines.say: [menacing] Your sword. Or your life.
Night after night. Nine hundred and ninety-nine swords.
[hushed] Then, on the last night... a boy walked onto the bridge. Playing a flute.
[worried] Oh no. Run, kid!
The boy didn't run. Up on Mount Kurama, he'd been trained... by the king of the tengu.
[raspy, fierce] Faster, boy. AGAIN!
[fast, intense] Benkei swung. The boy leapt onto the railing, flipped over his head, and knocked him flat. With a fan.
cap: The boy leapt onto the railing,

lines.say: [disbelief] He lost to a KID?!
[softer] Benkei got up... and bowed. From that night on, he served the boy. For life.
That boy was Minamoto no Yoshitsune. He grew up to be the greatest general Japan had ever seen.
[building] He charged horses down a cliff. He crushed his enemies at sea. Benkei by his side, every time.
[dark] Then his own brother, the future shogun, got jealous... and ordered him hunted.
They ran. At one checkpoint, Benkei beat his own master with a stick... to prove he was just a servant.
cap: to prove he was just a servant.

lines.say: [quiet] That's... so sad.
[grave] Finally, they were trapped. Yoshitsune went inside, for the last time. Benkei stood on the bridge. Alone.
[roaring] NO ONE CROSSES!
[intense] They sent wave after wave. He cut them all down. So they shot him. Again. And again.
[slow] Then it went quiet. He didn't fall. He didn't move. Nobody dared cross.
[hushed] When one finally crept closer... Benkei toppled over. He'd died standing up.
[sniffling] Okay. I'm actually crying.
[warm] Japan still calls your shin Benkei's crying spot. The one place that made even him cry.
[sly] And some people swear Yoshitsune escaped... and became Genghis Khan.
[screaming] WAIT, WHAT?!
